topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets out the specific learning objectives.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutational Processes vs. Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational debate over whether cancer development is driven primarily by intrinsic 'bad luck' genetic processes or by external environmental and lifestyle exposures supported by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the role of viral and bacterial pathogens in oncogenesis, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma and the lymphoma belt as a detailed model.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which chemical mutagens, radiation, and non-mutagenic inflammatory promoters cause cellular transformation and tissue-specific malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and identify mutational signatures.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with closing remarks on evaluating carcinogenic risk versus practical benefits in everyday decisions.
